title: Settings: fix missing accessible names and headings

confidence.rationale: Exact XAML assigns the version-only name and resources already label the outer group. This requests contextual wording as a nonblocking refinement, not a reproduced screen-reader defect.

proposed_comments.body:
### Give the version expander a localized purpose as well as its number

**Severity:** `low` (non-blocking accessible-name refinement)

The expander explicitly uses only `ViewModel.PowerToysVersion` as its accessible name. The surrounding **Version and updates** group already provides context, so this is not a claim that the current control is unnamed or that Narrator has been shown to fail. A contextual name on the expander itself would nevertheless make its purpose clearer when focus lands directly on it.

1. Add a localized format resource for the expander's name, such as `PowerToys version {0}`, to `Strings/en-us/Resources.resw`. Keep the version placeholder so translators control word order; do not concatenate an English prefix in XAML.
2. In `GeneralViewModel`, expose a formatted accessible-name property using the existing resource lookup mechanism and `PowerToysVersion`, then bind this expander's `AutomationProperties.Name` to it. Preserve the visible version header, preview badge, outer group's localized name and existing one-way binding behavior.
3. Check that the formatted name contains the current version and localized purpose. On an unlocked desktop, focus the expander with Narrator, expand/collapse it, and verify that the purpose, version and state remain clear without an unnecessary duplicate announcement. Include one non-English locale.

This refinement is separate from the shared color-picker and action-template bindings; their actual current headers are strings, so no object-to-type-name failure is alleged here.
proposed_comments.title: Give the version expander a localized purpose as well as its number
